prompt: A Bubble Tea program freezes for three seconds every time the user presses `r`, which reloads its data from a slow server. The `"r"` case of `Update` calls the function that fetches the data and stores the result in the model. What is the fix?
hint: Which part of a Bubble Tea program is allowed to take its time?

choices.text: Return a `tea.Cmd` that does the slow work and sends a message back
choices.why: Right. The program runs a command in a goroutine of its own, so `Update` returns at once, the screen keeps answering, and the data arrives later as a message `Update` handles.

choices.text: Move the fetch into `View`
choices.why: `View` runs after every `Update`, so the fetch would run on every key press, and a model changed there is a copy nobody keeps.

choices.text: Raise the frame rate with `tea.WithFPS(120)`
choices.why: The frame rate limits how often the screen is repainted. Nothing is repainted while `Update` is blocked, whatever the rate.

choices.text: Fetch in `Init` instead, once, before the first screen
choices.why: That moves the freeze to start-up and loses the reload. Slow work belongs in a command wherever it is asked for.

prompt: Code ported from a Bubble Tea v1 tutorial keeps `case tea.KeyMsg:` in `Update`. Built against `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` it works, until the view sets `KeyboardEnhancements.ReportEventTypes = true`; then, on a terminal that supports it, each press of `j` moves the cursor two rows. Why?
hint: What does `tea.KeyMsg` cover in version 2?

choices.text: The terminal repeats every key twice once enhancements are on
choices.why: The terminal sends one event when the key goes down and another when it comes up; neither is a repeat.

choices.text: In v2, `tea.KeyMsg` matches presses and releases alike
choices.why: Right. It became an interface over `tea.KeyPressMsg` and `tea.KeyReleaseMsg`; once releases are reported, both land in that case. Matching `tea.KeyPressMsg` fixes it.

choices.text: `View` is called twice per message when enhancements are on
choices.why: How often `View` runs does not move the cursor; only `Update` changes the model.

choices.text: `msg.String()` returns `"j j"` for an enhanced key
choices.why: The string is still `"j"`; the second move comes from a second message, the release.

choices.why: Right. Cron gives the job no terminal; a full-screen view has nothing to draw on and nobody to press a key.

choices.text: One of the operators uses a screen reader
choices.why: Right. A screen repainted cell by cell reaches a screen reader as fragments; printed lines arrive in order.

prompt: On a laptop, `go build -o hits .` for the `hits` tool takes 0.078 seconds. On a CI runner that starts from a clean machine for every job, the same build takes about 6 seconds each time. What explains the difference?
hint: Think about where compiled packages are kept between builds.

choices.text: CI machines compile without optimisation
choices.why: Nothing in the job changes compiler flags; and unoptimised builds are faster, not slower.

choices.text: The build cache is empty on every job, so the standard library is compiled again each time
choices.why: Right. A build from an empty `GOCACHE` compiled 79 packages in 5.8 s; the warm one compiled none. Keeping `GOCACHE` between jobs removes most of the gap.

choices.text: `-o` is slower when the output directory is new
choices.why: Writing one 4 MB file takes milliseconds; the seconds are compilation.

choices.text: The runner downloads Go's standard library from the module proxy
choices.why: The standard library ships with the toolchain in `GOROOT`; only modules come from the proxy, and `hits` requires none.

prompt: An old codebase writes `interface{}` everywhere. What does `gofmt -r 'interface{} -> any' -w .` do to it?
hint: Which identifiers in a rewrite rule are wildcards?

choices.text: Nothing: the rule fails, because `interface{}` is a type rather than an expression
choices.why: A type is a valid expression for a rewrite rule; the rule runs and rewrites every occurrence.

choices.text: Replaces every `interface{}` with `any`
choices.why: Right. Only single lowercase letters are wildcards, so `any` is taken literally, and `interface{}` becomes `any` in parameters, slices and literals alike.

choices.text: Replaces each `interface{}` with whatever expression `a` matched
choices.why: `any` is three letters, so it is not a wildcard; there is also no `a` in the pattern for it to refer to.

choices.text: Only the `interface{}` written in function parameters
choices.why: The rule matches the syntax wherever it appears: parameters, return types and composite literals.

choices.why: Tab width is an editor display setting; neither `gopls` nor `goimports` writes anything different because of it.

prompt: `ids := []int{1, 1, 2, 3, 3}; slices.Compact(ids); fmt.Println(ids)` compiles and `go vet` reports `result of slices.Compact call not used`. What does it print on Go 1.27.1?

choices.text: `[1 1 2 3 3]`, since the call changed nothing

prompt: A Go service runs with `GOMEMLIMIT=300MiB`. Its `GODEBUG=gctrace=1` lines read like `gc 812 @95.1s 31%: ... 310->312->305 MB, 310 MB goal`, one every few milliseconds, and requests have slowed to half speed. What is the right first change?
hint: Compare the live heap, the third heap number, with the limit.

choices.text: Lower `GOGC` so that each collection has less garbage to find
choices.why: There is almost no garbage to find: 305 of 312 MB survived. A lower `GOGC` only adds collections to a program already collecting continuously.

choices.text: Call `runtime.GC()` from a ticker every second
choices.why: A forced collection frees exactly what an automatic one frees, which here is nearly nothing, and adds stops of its own.

choices.text: Raise the limit above the live heap
choices.why: Right. The trace counts in units of 2^20 bytes, so 305 MB alive is already past the 300 MiB limit: every cycle frees nothing and the next starts at once. Keeping less alive would work too. Until then, the CPU limiter is all that keeps it at half speed rather than zero.

choices.why: Only the limit is triggering them already, and the limit is the problem: with the live heap above it, `GOGC=off` changes nothing.
